evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/ai-chat/hooks/useAiChat.ts:30-46 — the shared apiFetch() helper calls raw `fetch(url, { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...options?.headers } })` and NEVER attaches an `Authorization: Bearer` header. Every AI-chat endpoint is authenticated and lives under API_BASE `/api/v1/ai/chat` (:19), so all six hooks that go through apiFetch — useAiChatSessions (:53), useAiChatSession (:68), useAiChatMessages (:80), useCreateSession (:96), useSendMessage (:113), useMessageFeedback (:148), useEscalatedMessages (:165) — send requests with NO bearer token. ppt-web authenticates by injecting a localStorage bearer token (AuthContext + lib/api.ts request interceptor); a bare fetch carries none, so the api-server returns 401 and the entire AI-chat feature is non-functional for authenticated users.

This is confirmed by the in-repo reference implementation: features/notification-analytics/hooks/useNotificationAnalytics.ts:7-9 and :35-41 reads `ppt_access_token` from localStorage and sets `Authorization: Bearer ${token}` with the explicit comment 'the handler requires authentication — a bare fetch would 401'; features/sentiment/hooks/useSentiment.ts routes through getApiClient() precisely so 'the shared axios interceptors apply: Bearer-token injection' (:17-20). useAiChat.ts does neither. It is the SAME defect class already filed and FIXED for person-months/useBuildingUnits (backlog code-review-ppt-web-core-raw-fetch-bypasses-jwt-interceptor, status done) — recurring here in a file that fix never touched.

Second, distinct bug in the same file: useDeleteSession (:131-142) calls `await fetch(`${API_BASE}/sessions/${sessionId}`, { method: 'DELETE' })` at :136 with NO headers AND — unlike apiFetch — NO `response.ok` check. So a failed DELETE (401 from the missing token, 403, network error) neither throws nor rejects: the mutation resolves as success and onSuccess (:138) invalidates the sessions query, so the UI reports the session deleted when it was not (silent destructive-action failure). Landable frontend-only remedy: route all AI-chat calls through getApiClient() (preferred — inherits bearer injection, 401->refresh replay, ErrorResponse->ApiError, retry) or attach the localStorage bearer token as notification-analytics does, and make useDeleteSession share apiFetch so it checks response.ok. Verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/web typecheck` + a Vitest/RTL test asserting the request carries an Authorization header and that a rejected DELETE surfaces an error. Confidence high: traced from apiFetch through the auth transport (localStorage bearer) and confirmed against the sibling files that document the 401.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/meters/hooks/useOcrMeterReading.ts:26-35 — the ocrFetch() helper calls raw `fetch(url, options)` and attaches NO `Authorization: Bearer` header (callers pass only a Content-Type at :60-62 for the correction POST, and nothing at all for the multipart upload). Both endpoints are authenticated api-server routes under API_BASE `/api/v1/ai` (:11): useOcrProcessImage POSTs multipart to `/api/v1/ai/ocr/meter-reading` (:45) and useOcrCorrection POSTs JSON to `/api/v1/ai/ocr/correction` (:59). ppt-web authenticates via a localStorage bearer token that only lib/api.ts's axios interceptor injects; a bare fetch carries none, so both OCR calls 401 and the OCR meter-reading feature (Epic 128) never works for a real signed-in user.

Same raw-fetch-bypasses-JWT class as the flagship ai-chat finding and as the already-FIXED person-months finding (backlog code-review-ppt-web-core-raw-fetch-bypasses-jwt-interceptor, done). Correct in-repo pattern to copy: features/sentiment/hooks/useSentiment.ts routes through getApiClient() so the shared interceptors inject the bearer token; features/notification-analytics/hooks/useNotificationAnalytics.ts:35-41 attaches the localStorage token manually with the comment 'a bare fetch would 401'. The hook does at least expose processingError/correctionError (:98-99) so the component can render the failure — but the failure is guaranteed on every call, not incidental. Landable frontend-only remedy: replace ocrFetch with getApiClient() (multipart is supported by axios) or attach the bearer token; medium severity because the whole feature path is broken but the error is at least surfaced to the caller. Verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/web typecheck` + a Vitest test asserting the OCR request carries an Authorization header. Confidence high: traced the auth transport and confirmed against the sibling reference hooks.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/OrganizationProvider.tsx:8-12 — the context value is built as a fresh object literal on every render (`const value = user?.organizationId ? { organizationId, organizationName } : null`) and passed straight into <OrganizationContext.Provider value={value}>. Because OrganizationProvider consumes useAuth() and re-renders on every AuthContext change, a NEW object identity is handed to the context on each render, so every component subscribed via useOrganization() (hooks/useOrganization.ts) re-renders even when organizationId/organizationName are unchanged.

This diverges from the app's own established pattern: every other provider in this segment memoizes its context value — contexts/AuthContext.tsx wraps its value in useMemo (:689-712) and contexts/WebSocketContext.tsx does the same (:392-405), each with the explicit comment 'Memoize the context value to prevent unnecessary re-renders'. OrganizationProvider is the lone provider that does not. Landable frontend-only remedy: wrap the value in useMemo keyed on [user?.organizationId, user?.organizationName] (returning null when no org). Low severity (+1, render-perf/consistency smell, not a correctness crash). Verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/web typecheck` + a Vitest render-count test. Confidence medium: the missing memoization is confirmed by static read and by contrast with the sibling providers; the runtime re-render impact scales with how many components consume useOrganization().
